mos-small-signal-model.L1: Draws the saturated MOSFET model: a current source g_m·v_gs from drain to source, r_o across it, and no gate current.
mos-small-signal-model.L2: Substitutes the model into a single-transistor circuit and solves it, with g_m and r_o computed from the bias.
mos-small-signal-model.L3: Explains each part: g_m·v_gs is the tangent's slope, r_o = 1/(λI_D) the slope of i_D against v_DS, and the open gate the insulating oxide; says why the model is the same for every circuit while its numbers change with the bias.
mos-small-signal-model.L4: Adds g_mb for a source not at the body potential and the capacitances for high frequency; knows the model holds only in saturation and for v_gs ≪ V_OV.
missteps: adds a resistor between gate and source in the MOSFET model
uses the small-signal model without checking that the transistor is in saturation
draws the current source pointing the wrong way for v_gs
uses r_o = 1/(λI_D) with λ = 0 and gets zero instead of infinity

seeds.predict: Two transistors carry the same current, one at twice the V_OV of the other. Compare their g_m and r_o.
seeds.explain: Why there is no resistor between gate and source in the MOSFET model.
seeds.limit: λ made smaller and smaller: what does r_o become, and what is the transistor then?
seeds.transfer: A PMOS common-source stage with its source on V_DD: draw its small-signal circuit and compare it with the NMOS one.
